question: A 15-year-old teenager presents for a sports physical. His blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg, temperature is 36.5°C (97.7°F), and heart rate is 100/min. On cardiac auscultation, an early diastolic heart sound is heard over the cardiac apex while the patient is in the left lateral decubitus position. A transthoracic echocardiogram is performed which shows an ejection fraction of 60% without any other abnormalities. Which of the following is the end-systolic volume in this patient if his cardiac output is 6 L/min?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Cardiac output is 6 L/min" -> "Cardiac output = Stroke volume x Heart rate" -> "Stroke volume = Cardiac output / Heart rate" -> "Stroke volume = 6 L/min / 100 beats/min" -> "Stroke volume = 0.06 L/beat" -> "End-systolic volume = Stroke volume" -> "End-systolic volume = 60 mL" -> 100%
analysis: The end-systolic volume (ESV) can be calculated using the formula: Cardiac Output (CO) = Stroke Volume (SV) x Heart Rate (HR). Given that CO = 6 L/min and ejection fraction = 60%, SV = 60% of end-diastolic volume (EDV). Therefore, ESV = EDV - SV. Since EF = SV/EDV, EDV = SV/EF. Substituting the values, we can calculate ESV.
